email.subject1: pipeline Origence is leaving on the table
email.body1:
Sean, saw Origence's CUDL network funded $48B in auto loans in 2025 and is expanding eContracting across new markets into 2026.

Growth like that usually means more credit unions and dealers worth covering than an inside sales team can touch before the rollout lands. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a personalized signal play for Origence off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Sean, quick follow-up for Origence.

With eContracting expanding, the number of accounts in play often jumps faster than an inside team can ramp. Most teams don't actually know how many meetings they need to book to cover that, so the gap shows up late in the quarter.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I'll walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings Origence needs to close that coverage gap, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Sean, last bit of proof for Origence.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and couldn't hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks with every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Origence's reply rate likely compares to other lending-tech teams. Want to hop on a quick call and I'll walk you through it?
email.body4:
Sean, I'll stop reaching out on this one, but didn't want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling coverage without adding inside reps isn't a priority while the 2026 rollouts are in motion, no problem at all. Timing is everything, and a platform launch is its own kind of busy.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to an inside sales motion? I'll tailor it to Origence either way.
